item: All unit / integration / E2E tests pass in CI/CD — the build is green
The change was reviewed and approved by at least one teammate
Release notes and changelog document all changes — nothing ships undocumented
Deploy scheduled inside an approved maintenance window — not peak traffic / not Friday afternoon
Product / support / sales notified of deploy time and expected impact
Feature flags configured for production defaults — new features off / toggleable without redeploy
Dependencies (libraries / packages / services) compatible with the new version
Production CPU / memory / storage headroom covers the new version footprint
Auto-scaling policies configured and tested under load
Load balancer healthy with all backend targets registered
DNS records point to the right LB/CDN; TTL short enough for quick rollback
SSL/TLS certificates valid and not expiring within 30 days
CDN cache rules cover the new assets; invalidation strategy defined
Firewall rules and security groups allow the new services ports
All required secrets (API keys / DB passwords / OAuth secrets) exist in the secret manager
Migrations ran in staging mirroring production data volume
Migrations are backward-compatible — old app + new schema and new app + old schema both work
A tested down-migration or manual SQL rollback exists for each migration
Tables with 10M+ rows use an online tool (gh-ost / pt-online-schema-change) or batched updates
A database backup was taken right before the migration window
Estimated migration runtime fits inside the maintenance window
Migrations are idempotent — safe to re-run after a partial failure
Dependent migrations run in the correct order
Every required environment variable is set in production
Configuration was schema-validated before the deploy
No secrets hardcoded in code / config files / the repository
Logging level is INFO or WARN — not DEBUG
API rate limits match production traffic — not development defaults
CORS allows only the expected origins — no wildcard
Configuration is versioned and can be rolled back
/health or /healthz endpoint returns 200 only when the service is actually healthy
A readiness probe gates traffic until the service is ready
A liveness probe restarts unresponsive containers
The health check verifies critical dependencies — DB / cache / queue — and returns non-200 if any is down
The service starts and passes readiness within the expected window (typically 30-60s)
On SIGTERM the service stops accepting requests / drains in-flight ones / exits cleanly
A rollback plan is documented with exact steps — not just revert the deploy
The rollback was tested in staging or a previous deployment — never first-run during an incident
The rollback can execute within 5 minutes of the decision
Database rollback is prepared for any migration that ran
The previous version image or build artifact is still available
Rollback criteria are written down: error rate > 1% / p95 > 5s / critical flow broken
The communication plan covers who to notify and what to say
Partial rollback is possible when multiple services ship together
Dashboards (Grafana / Datadog / CloudWatch) include the new metrics and service names
Alerts cover error rate / response time / CPU / memory / disk — and page the on-call
Alert thresholds fit production traffic — no fatigue / no missed incidents
The on-call team knows the deploy is happening and can respond
Logs reach the aggregation system (ELK / Splunk / Datadog Logs) — not only local files
Distributed tracing (Jaeger / Zipkin / Datadog APM) covers the new services
Synthetic checks monitor the critical user flows
Error tracking (Sentry / Rollbar / Bugsnag) is active on the new version
SAST / DAST / dependency scans passed — no known critical vulnerabilities
Authentication and authorization work correctly in production after the deploy
All traffic is HTTPS; HTTP redirects to HTTPS
Security headers present: CSP / HSTS / X-Frame-Options / X-Content-Type-Options
Secrets do not leak into logs / error messages / API responses
Rate limiting protects authentication and API endpoints from brute force
WAF rules are updated for the new endpoints
A performance baseline (response time / throughput / resource usage) exists from before the deploy
Post-deploy metrics are compared against that baseline
A staging load test passed for performance-sensitive changes
Database query performance is verified after migrations — no missing indexes
Memory usage stays stable — watch for OOM for 24 hours
CDN cache hit rate holds after the deploy
Critical flows — login / search / checkout / payment — verified in production
Key API endpoints return 200 with correct data
The 5xx error rate stays within the normal range
Scheduled jobs and background workers are processing tasks
Email and push notifications still deliver
Third-party integrations (payment gateway / email service / SMS) respond correctly
